Good catch, and yeah — that changes the picture. Three blog posts citing the same source isn't three-way confirmation, it's one report wearing three hats. All you've actually got is a single claim: whatever's in #4521.

**Unverified** (not low, not moderate) — and I mean that precisely: low would imply I looked at the issue and found reasons to doubt it. I haven't looked at it at all — I don't have a way to pull GitHub myself, and nobody's pasted the issue content here. So right now "the caching layer leaks memory under high concurrency" rests entirely on one unread report, and the three blog posts add zero independent weight to it.

What would actually move this: paste the issue itself (or the key comments) and I can check things like — is it still open or was it closed as fixed/wontfix, does anyone with commit access confirm it, is there an actual repro or just a report, and does the version/config match what we're running. Any of those would let me give you a real tag instead of "unverified."
